where: Section 3, paragraph on upper and lower bounds
problem: The example 'For B = {4, 6} the only upper bound is 12 ... the lower bounds are 1 and 2, so GLB = 2' does not say which poset it is working in. The paragraph just before uses the poset {2, 3, 4, 6}, and in that poset {4, 6} has no upper bound at all and only 2 as a lower bound (1 is not in the set). A student reading straight through gets the wrong numbers.
fix: Name the ambient poset: 'In A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12} under divisibility, for B = {4, 6} the only upper bound is 12, so LUB = 12; the lower bounds are 1 and 2, so GLB = 2. In the smaller poset {2, 3, 4, 6}, {4, 6} has no upper bound and only the lower bound 2.'

problem: 'Height' appears for the first time in the final step and is not defined anywhere in the chapter; textbooks also differ, some counting elements of the longest chain and some counting its edges.
fix: Define it before using it: 'The height of a poset is the number of elements in its longest chain (some books call the number of edges the length and count one less). Here 1 ≺ 2 ≺ 4 ≺ 12 has 4 elements, so the height is 4.'

problem: The definition of comparable and incomparable is repeated word for word from Section 1, which makes the student think a new distinction is being introduced.
fix: Drop the repetition and start directly with the antichain: 'A subset whose elements are pairwise incomparable is an antichain.'
